findings.title: AWS secret access key
findings.description: A 40-character secret appears next to an AWS secret-key identifier.
findings.remediation: Revoke and rotate this credential, then load it from an environment variable or a secrets manager.

findings.title: Stripe live secret key
findings.description: String matches the format of a live Stripe secret or restricted key.
findings.remediation: Revoke and rotate this credential, then load it from an environment variable or a secrets manager.

findings.title: GitHub token
findings.description: String matches the format of a GitHub personal access or app token.
findings.remediation: Revoke and rotate this credential, then load it from an environment variable or a secrets manager.

findings.title: Private key block
findings.description: A PEM/OpenSSH/PGP private key header was found in source.
findings.remediation: Remove the key from the repository, rotate it, and purge it from git history.

findings.title: Credentials in URL
findings.description: A URL embeds a username and password.
findings.remediation: Move credentials out of connection strings into configuration or a secrets manager.

findings.title: SQL built with string formatting
findings.description: A query is assembled with f-strings, %, .format() or concatenation, which allows SQL injection. Value is interpolated directly into the query text.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries, e.g. cursor.execute('... WHERE id = ?', (user_id,)).

findings.title: SQL built with string formatting
findings.snippet: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '%s'" % uid)
findings.description: A query is assembled with f-strings, %, .format() or concatenation, which allows SQL injection. Value is interpolated directly into the query text.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries, e.g. cursor.execute('... WHERE id = ?', (user_id,)).

findings.title: SQL built with string formatting
findings.snippet: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + uid + "'")
findings.description: A query is assembled with f-strings, %, .format() or concatenation, which allows SQL injection. Value is interpolated directly into the query text.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries, e.g. cursor.execute('... WHERE id = ?', (user_id,)).

findings.title: SQL built with string formatting
findings.description: A query is assembled with f-strings, %, .format() or concatenation, which allows SQL injection. Value is interpolated directly into the query text.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries, e.g. cursor.execute('... WHERE id = ?', (user_id,)).

findings.title: SQL built with string formatting
findings.description: A query is assembled with f-strings, %, .format() or concatenation, which allows SQL injection. Query variable 'query' was built with string formatting.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries, e.g. cursor.execute('... WHERE id = ?', (user_id,)).

findings.title: Use of eval()
findings.description: eval() executes arbitrary Python from a string and enables code injection.
findings.remediation: Use ast.literal_eval() for literals, or parse input with a purpose-built parser.

findings.title: subprocess with shell=True
findings.description: Running commands through a shell exposes the call to command injection.
findings.remediation: Pass an argument list and leave shell=False.

findings.title: Unsafe deserialization (pickle/marshal/shelve)
findings.description: Unpickling untrusted data can execute arbitrary code.
findings.remediation: Use JSON or another data-only format; sign and verify data if pickle is unavoidable.

findings.title: yaml.load without a safe loader
findings.description: yaml.load with the default or full loader can construct arbitrary objects.
findings.remediation: Use yaml.safe_load() or pass Loader=yaml.SafeLoader.

findings.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
findings.description: verify=False allows man-in-the-middle attacks.
findings.remediation: Leave verification on; supply a CA bundle path if you need a private CA.

findings.title: Use of exec()
findings.description: exec() executes arbitrary Python from a string and enables code injection.
findings.remediation: Avoid dynamic code execution; dispatch through an explicit mapping of allowed functions.

findings.title: AWS access key ID
findings.description: String matches the format of an AWS access key ID.
findings.remediation: Revoke and rotate this credential, then load it from an environment variable or a secrets manager. Prefer IAM roles over long-lived keys.

findings.title: Google API key
findings.description: String matches the format of a Google API key.
findings.remediation: Revoke and rotate this credential, then load it from an environment variable or a secrets manager. Restrict the key by API and referrer in Google Cloud.

findings.title: Slack token
findings.description: String matches the format of a Slack API token.
findings.remediation: Revoke and rotate this credential, then load it from an environment variable or a secrets manager.

findings.title: Hardcoded password or secret
findings.description: A credential-like variable is assigned a high-entropy string literal.
findings.remediation: Revoke and rotate this credential, then load it from an environment variable or a secrets manager.

findings.title: Hardcoded credential in assignment
findings.snippet: ADMIN_PASSWORD = "letmein"  # too short for the regex pass; the AST pass catches it
findings.description: A credential-like variable is assigned a non-empty string constant. Variable 'ADMIN_PASSWORD' holds a string literal.
findings.remediation: Revoke and rotate this credential, then load it from an environment variable or a secrets manager.

findings.title: os.system / os.popen call
findings.description: Shell command execution is vulnerable to command injection when input is untrusted.
findings.remediation: Use subprocess.run() with an argument list.

findings.title: Weak hash algorithm (MD5/SHA-1)
findings.description: MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for security purposes.
findings.remediation: Use SHA-256 or better; use bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 for passwords.

findings.title: Insecure temporary file (mktemp)
findings.description: tempfile.mktemp() is subject to race conditions.
findings.remediation: Use tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() or tempfile.mkstemp().

findings.title: Debug mode enabled
findings.description: Running a web framework with debug=True can expose an interactive debugger.
findings.remediation: Disable debug mode in production and drive it from configuration.

findings.title: Insecure random for security use
findings.description: The random module is not cryptographically secure.
findings.remediation: Use the secrets module for tokens, passwords and keys.

findings.title: assert used for a check
findings.description: assert statements are stripped when Python runs with -O, so checks vanish.
findings.remediation: Raise an explicit exception for validation and authorization checks.

findings.title: Binding to all network interfaces
findings.description: Binding to 0.0.0.0 exposes the service on every interface.
findings.remediation: Bind to 127.0.0.1 unless external access is intended and protected.

findings.title: Bare except clause
findings.description: A bare except hides errors, including security-relevant ones.
findings.remediation: Catch specific exception types.
